chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Jenkins Orphanage musicians
summary: He says Armstrong never mentioned the orphanage; Jabbo Smith and Cat Anderson came from there.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I'd like to ask one question of J. C. that I had in the back of my mind. In all of your younger travels, when you met Louis Armstrong, did Louis Armstrong ever talk about the Jenkins Orphanage; did any musicians?
Never mentioned it.
The Jenkins Orphanage was a pretty famous and is today still a pretty famous orphanage in South Carolina, Charleston, South Carolina.
Never mentioned it.
It turned out a lot of great musicians.
I know. It turned out the best.
Do you know some of the musicians who came out of the Jenkins Orphanage?
Louis never mentioned it. We were like this ... all the time I was together with him and he never mentioned, never did.
Do you know of any of the musicians who came out of the Jenkins Orphanage?
Jabbo Smith. Jabberwocky, he came from there.

Yes. One of the best. He played trombone and trumpet and played. He played down at the Small's and let's see who else. That's about all I remember. But, every kid that came out of their orphanage played.
Well, Coot Anderson came out of that orphanage.
Oh, he did? That I didn't know. And I've known Coot a long time.
It turned out a lot of trumpet players.
He's a great trumpet player. He used to live next to my sister in the Bronx. I used to see him quite often.
Oh, yeah?
Yeah, that's before my sister moved ...
He lives in California now.
No, I mean he lived in the Bronx?
Oh, yeah. ... see my sister.
He lived right next to Red, didn't he?
No. He lived on Church, is that Church Street? What is that street there? On the corner of Prospect and what? He lived on Holmes Street.
Did you know Gil Askey?
I did but not that much.
Gil Askey was the person who did the arrangement on 'Good Morning Heartache' that's being played on the radio right now.
... (too many talking and too far away)
